turns.text: Hey Simone. Really glad we could do this. It's funny, looking at your projects—welding, robots that playfully slap people in the face—there's this intense, beautiful curiosity behind the chaos.

turns.innerMonologue: Okay, he laughed right away. The serious black-suit guy actually has a warm sense of humor. That's a huge relief.

turns.text: Guilty as charged. I do stare at the ceiling, but usually I'm wondering what consciousness actually is, or if my guitar playing sounds like sad Dostoevsky. But I love how you took Truckla and just built it because nobody else would. That kind of creative fearlessness is so rare.

turns.text: Well, Truckla almost gave me three nervous breakdowns, but seeing people's faces on the freeway made every single bruised knuckle worth it. What about you? When you're sitting with someone for 4 hours on the podcast, what makes you feel like you truly connected with them?
turns.innerMonologue: He's listening with his whole face. He hasn't looked at his phone once. That's so rare in this city.

turns.text: It's the moment when the public persona drops. When someone admits they're scared, or that they really love something stupid. Life is heavy, but sharing a genuine laugh with someone who gets it... that's kind of everything, isn't it?
turns.innerMonologue: Chemistry is clicking on every level. We're both suckers for earnest vulnerability.

turns.text: Couldn't agree more, Lex. Look, next time we should skip the fancy drinks—come by the workshop, I'll teach you how to weld, and you can teach me a song on the guitar. Deal?
turns.innerMonologue: Definitely want a second date. He's authentic, kind, and grounded.
